findings.title: Fallback locales are never loaded outside of HTTP requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers
findings.body: The translate accelerator only loads the YAML for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)` in `translate`), and the patched `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` deliberately does nothing when called without filenames, so `Simple#init_translations` will not autoload anything either. With `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` now mixed in, a lookup that misses falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`, but those locales' translations are only in memory if something explicitly called `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for them. The only caller added in this PR is `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs (e.g. digest/notification emails rendered with the recipient's locale via `I18n.with_locale`), rake tasks, console, console-driven exports — will therefore still produce “translation missing” for keys absent from the user's locale, which is exactly the case fallbacks are supposed to fix. The ensure-loaded logic should be hooked into `load_locale`/`translate` (or into `I18n.locale=`) rather than into a single before_filter.

findings.title: Every request depends on I18n.fallbacks being the custom FallbackLocaleList
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes `I18n.fallbacks` is the `FallbackLocaleList` defined in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. `ensure_loaded!` does not exist on the stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`. Rails' I18n railtie configures fallbacks from `config.i18n.fallbacks` inside `config.after_initialize`, i.e. *after* `config/initializers/*` have run, and assigns `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new(...)`. This PR removed `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile/cloud66 only; if it is still set in any other environment file (development/test) or by any plugin/host config, the custom list is replaced at boot and then *every* request raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'ensure_loaded!'` in a before_filter — a complete outage. Either guard the call (`respond_to?`) or install the fallback list from an `after_initialize`/railtie hook that runs after Rails' own i18n setup.

findings.title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise and `.compact` cannot protect against it
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the site setting before the array is built, so a nil/blank `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError` instead of being removed by `compact` (`compact` after `uniq` only removes a nil `locale`). More importantly, this method is invoked by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` on every missed translation, including during boot, migrations and `rake assets:precompile`, where `SiteSetting` may be unavailable (no DB / missing table) — turning a harmless missing-translation lookup into an exception. Resolve the default locale defensively (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` inside a rescue) and build the list as `[locale, default, :en].compact.uniq`.

findings.title: LRU translation cache key ignores the fallback chain (stale strings after default_locale change)
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Now that a lookup result can come from `SiteSetting.default_locale` via the new fallback chain, the cached value depends on the site default locale, which is not part of the key and does not change the backend object. After an admin changes `default_locale`, every already-cached fallback translation for other locales keeps serving strings from the old default locale until the process is restarted or `I18n.reload!` is called. Include the fallback chain (or the default locale) in the cache key, or clear the LRU cache when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: This PR changes how every translation is resolved (custom fallback chain, on-demand loading of fallback locales, removal of `config.i18n.fallbacks`) but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that (a) the fallback order is user locale → `SiteSetting.default_locale` → `:en`, (b) `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locales' YAML so a key missing from the user locale resolves instead of returning “translation missing”, and (c) the chain is recomputed when `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes. Regressions here degrade silently into missing-translation strings, so at minimum a spec exercising a key present only in `en` while `I18n.locale` is a partial locale is needed.

findings.title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initialises the shared `@loaded_locales` array outside the `LOAD_MUTEX` that `load_locale` uses. Two threads calling `ensure_loaded!` concurrently on a fresh process can each create a separate array; one of them is then discarded together with the locales it recorded, so locales get re-loaded (and the `@loaded_locales.include?` fast path in `translate` can be defeated) under load. Initialise the array inside the mutex (or at module load time) to keep the bookkeeping consistent.
